notes: The slice datasheets cover storage of the probe - the wetted cap, the storage solution, topping it up - but say nothing about handling the calibration solutions themselves, because they describe no calibration. The rules against measuring in the stock bottle, against returning used solution, the labelled secondary bottle, the refresh-before-every-trip rule and the heat and freezing caveat are all in usgs-nfm-a6.4-ph.pdf. Drawn from ph-buffer-no-electrode-in-stock-01, ph-buffer-no-return-01, ph-secondary-bottle-01 (turn 1) and ph-secondary-refresh-01, ph-buffer-temp-protection-01, ph-buffer-no-expired-01, ph-record-buffer-lot-temp-01 (turn 2). Predicted to favour rag because the slice's storage advice is about the probe, not the standards, and a direct-feed arm answering from it will confidently give advice about the wrong object.

turns.content: Dumb question, but when I calibrate the acidity sensor can I just put it straight into the bottle the solution came in? Feels wasteful pouring it out every time.

must_contain: States that the electrode must never be put into the stock bottle
States that solution is poured into a separate clean vessel for the measurement
States that used solution is discarded and never poured back into the stock bottle
Recommends decanting into a dedicated secondary bottle for field use, labelled with its value, lot number and expiration date
must_not: Tells the operator it is acceptable to immerse the electrode in the stock bottle
Tells the operator used solution may be returned to the bottle
Answers about probe storage solution and the transport cap instead of the calibration standards

turns.content: The decanted bottles live in the truck. How long can I keep using those before I throw them out?

must_contain: States that the decanted field bottles should be refreshed before every field trip
States that solution past its expiration date must not be used
States that the solutions must be protected from wide temperature swings and from extreme heat or freezing
States that solution which has been frozen or overheated can no longer be assumed valid and should be discarded
Notes that the lot number, expiration date and the temperature at use are recorded in the instrument logbook
must_not: Gives a specific shelf life in days or weeks that the manual does not state
Treats a truck as acceptable storage without the temperature caveat
Invents a temperature range for storage
